scope: every saved episode file under runs/*/episodes, runs/*/replaced and runs/*/superseded (4,169 files) as they stood at the time of the scan; another agent was writing episode files at the same time, so episodes saved after about 19:44 UTC on 16 Nov 2026 are not included. The scan's scripts were one-off scripts outside this repository (pass1.py, own.py, hits.py, tmpreads2.py, exposure.py, foreign_tmp.py, net.py); each check's `method` field says what it did.

check1_other_episode_checkout_names_in_t.method: Every tool result in `messages` (full text) was searched for checkout folder names (`w` + 10 hex digits as a whole word). Each episode's own folder is the name shown by the most tool calls that show exactly one such name (at least 2:1 over the runner-up); broad listings that show many names at once are not used as evidence. Every name owned by a saved episode was then mapped back to that episode, so a name in another episode's result can be attributed. No name was claimed as own by two episodes. Toy-task episodes have no w-folder; their sandbox folders (named after the episode) were searched for separately.

check1b_laptop_files_directly_under_tmp.method: For laptop episodes only: each /tmp (or /private/tmp) entry named in a command or read_file call was followed through the episode. An entry counts as 'not created by this episode' when its first mention is a read or listing (cat/head/tail/grep/ls/... or Python open/load) and not a write in the same command (redirect, tee, -o/--out, mkdir, cp/mv target, write_text, write_file). All candidates were then read by hand. Separately, files the episode DID write and then read back in a later call were checked against every laptop episode running at an overlapping time that wrote a file of the same name; for those reads the result was searched for another task's package or folder name.
